{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** Legal (In-House Counsel)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — issues, positions and next steps

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The commercial architecture is workable in several respects, but the risk allocation is materially one-sided against us in four critical or high-risk areas, three of which sit at or near our walk-away thresholds.

The single most serious gap is the **complete absence of an indemnification section**. The outline runs from Section 19 (Warranties) directly to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), so there is no Vendor defence or indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data compromise, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Several surviving clauses assume that section exists — §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-reference indemnity concepts — leaving dangling references that must be repaired.

We also face an **inverted intellectual property position**: § 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of bespoke Deliverables in the Vendor and leaves us a revocable, non-transferable licence expiring with the Order Form term, meaning we lose access to work product we paid for. Separately, the Agreement loads a cluster of **one-way restrictive covenants onto us** — a reverse most-favoured-nation disclose-and-match obligation (§ 7.2), a 24-month worldwide non-compete and a 24-month no-hire (§ 12.4) — each of which contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor expressly acknowledges we made no such commitments. That internal inconsistency strengthens our deletion arguments considerably. Finally, § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights," with no offsetting termination for convenience anywhere in Section 9.

On the positive side, the limitation of liability package (Section 21), assignment and change-of-control provisions (Section 24), audit rights (Section 22), renewal mechanics (Section 8), insurance (Section 18) and the liquidated-damages position all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline. Governing law is a straightforward fix: § 28.1 selects Singapore but directly conflicts with § 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts.

One finding — the warranty analysis under Section 19 — did not clear verification and is flagged for review before we rely on it.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 19.5 (gap where § 20 should sit) | No indemnification provision at all; §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 contain dangling cross-references. Insert new Section 20 with Vendor defence/indemnity for IP, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; narrow Customer indemnity; standard procedure; and § 20.5 remedies. No super-cap needed as § 21.3 already carves indemnification out of the cap. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns bespoke Deliverables; we get only a revocable, term-limited licence. Reverse so Customer owns paid-for Deliverables via present assignment, preserving Vendor Technology under § 14.3. Fallback: perpetual, irrevocable § 13.2-style licence over the whole Deliverable. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of trailing 12-month Fees or USD 1,000,000; Excluded Claims (§ 21.3) sit outside the cap and are uncapped. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Consent-free Customer assignment to Affiliate or M&A successor; Vendor bound by consent and competitor bar. No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Disclose-and-match obligation is a right of first refusal creating de facto exclusivity; compounds § 2.1 take-or-pay and contradicts § 12.3. Delete. Fallback: category-limited 12-month first-look, terminating on service-level or delivery failure. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 7.1 | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee; § 27.3 permits termination "without penalty." No redline. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 14.2 | Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable, term-limited and silent on Affiliates/contractors — inconsistent with §§ 13.1–13.3. Conform § 14.2 to the perpetual, irrevocable, transferable § 13.2/13.3 grant. |
| High | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Reverse MFN requiring us to surface and match third-party offers; contradicts § 12.3 and no Vendor-granted MFN exists to lose. Delete. Fallback: single defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | 24-month, worldwide, undefined-scope post-term non-compete binding us; exceeds 12-month walk-away limit and contradicts § 12.3. Delete. Fallback: named product, term-only plus 12 months, with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination) | Three-year term (§ 8.1) with cause-based termination only, against a § 2.1 take-or-pay with no reduction rights. Insert § 9.4: Customer convenience right on 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund, no penalty, overriding § 2.1, with no reciprocal Vendor right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, cost-shift only above 5% underpayment, no direct system access. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, outside the accepted list and conflicting with § 28.2 (New York County). Replace with New York law and delete the redundant Singapore venue grant so § 28.2 controls. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights"; conflicts with §§ 7.1 and 12.3. Replace with non-binding forecasts and Fees payable only for Services ordered or used. Fallback: 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire over every Vendor employee with no general-advertising or unsolicited-applicant carve-out; contradicts § 12.3. Delete. Fallback: mutual, 12 months, personnel directly involved, standard carve-outs, no no-hire. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension; § 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI or 3%. No redline. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.2 | No transition period, no data export in machine-readable format, no deletion or certification; § 16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11. Insert § 10.3: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 19.1 | Analysis concludes Section 19 meets or exceeds our preferred position and requires no redline, but this finding did not pass verification. To be re-confirmed before we rely on it. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL USD 1M/2M, workers' comp, employer's liability USD 1M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M for term plus one year; § 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability. No redline. |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following provisions sit at or approaching our stated walk-away positions. We should not sign without resolution.

1. **No Vendor IP indemnity (§ 20 absent).** The total absence of any Vendor defence or indemnity — including for third-party IP infringement — approaches the walk-away position. The dangling cross-references in §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 confirm the section was intended to exist.
2. **Deliverable licence terms (§ 14.2).** The revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence, silent on Affiliates and contractors, falls to the walk-away position on licence scope and is internally inconsistent with the perpetual, irrevocable grant we already have in §§ 13.2–13.3.
3. **Take-or-pay minimum commitment (§ 2.1).** A three-year USD 2,000,000-per-year commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights" is the walk-away formulation, and it conflicts with both § 7.1 and § 12.3.
4. **Reverse MFN (§ 7.2).** An open-ended obligation to extend Vendor better terms obtained from third parties is unacceptable and is contradicted by § 12.3.
5. **Non-compete (§ 12.4).** A 24-month, worldwide, undefined-scope restriction exceeds the 12-month limit and binds the wrong party.
6. **No-hire (§ 12.4).** A one-way 24-month no-hire with no general-advertising or unsolicited-applicant carve-out sits at the walk-away edge.
7. **Foreign governing law and venue (§ 28.1).** Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is close to the walk-away position, and is in any event irreconcilable with § 28.2.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** implementing the proposals above: insert Section 20 (Indemnification) with § 20.5 infringement remedies to repair the § 9.3 cross-reference; reverse ownership and conform the licence in § 14.2; insert § 9.4 (termination for convenience) and § 10.3 (transition assistance, data return, certified deletion); replace § 2.1; delete § 7.2 and § 12.4; and substitute New York law in § 28.1.
2. **Lead the covenant discussion with § 12.3.** Vendor's own acknowledgement that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment directly contradicts §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4. We should present these as drafting conflicts to be resolved in our favour rather than as negotiated concessions.
3. **Resolve the § 20 numbering gap with Vendor.** Confirm whether the indemnity section was omitted in error and request their standard language as a starting point, while tabling our own draft.
4. **Re-verify the WARRANTY finding (§ 19).** That finding failed verification; we will re-review Section 19 before confirming that no redline is required.
5. **Confirm the § 16.5 cross-reference.** Section 16.5 carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15," but Section 11 does not appear in the document. We will raise this with Vendor alongside the § 10.3 insertion.
6. **Hold the compliant provisions.** Sections 8, 18, 21, 22 and 24 meet or exceed our positions; we should resist any reopening of these as trade currency.
7. **Brief the business** on the § 2.1 and § 7.2 positions, since removing the take-or-pay and the disclose-and-match right materially changes the commercial model Vendor has proposed."}
